newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Friday:
Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said the Commission's weekly meeting would start at 0900/0800 GMT on Wednesday in Strasbourg.

Van der Pas also said the U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright would meet Commission President Jacques Santer and Commissioners Sir Leon Brittan, Hans van den Broek, Yves-Thibault de Silguy and Emma Bonino at 0930/0830 on Tuesday. He said Santer, Brittan and Albright would hold a news conference at 1020/0920 GMT.
Van der Pas said the Russia/EU summit would now be held on March 3 in Moscow.

Spokesman Jean-Christophe Filori said Commissioner Neil Kinnock had sent a letter to Spanish Development Minister Rafael Arias Salgado to express his concern about the deterioration of the road haulage sector dispute in Spain. Filori said the Commissioner had asked Salgado if Spain envisaged compensating non-Spanish hauliers whose lorries were damaged during the dispute, as France had done after experiencing the same problems.

Spokesman Patrick Child briefed on Monday's ECOFIN Council. He said the agenda would include the 1997 Commission economic report, Belgium's convergence programme and aid to Georgia, Armenia, Takjikistan and Macedonia.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/113: Car prices in the EU on 1 November 1996: lowest in the Netherlands, dearest in Germany.
- IP/97/121: The Commission approves management buy-in of Finnish Chemicals Oy.
- IP/97/122: Commissioner van den Broek meets Slovak Deputy Prime Minister Mrs Tothova.
- IP/97/124: Commissioner Neil Kinnock expresses strong concern about the situation in the road haulage dispute in Spain.
- IP/97/125: Information sociaty: the global inventory project (GIB) launches a web site.
- Speech/97/37: Speech by Commissioner Franz Fischler on the perspective in the European farm policy.
- General Report on the activities of the European Union in 1996.
- Eurostat memo No 1/97: EU records a surplus in trade in services of 11.7 Bn ECU in 1994.
